## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(plotly)
library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
library(mdsr)
library(sf)
library(ggspatial)
library(leaflet)
library(tidyverse)
```


When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
# Create sf object for US counties
full_data <- read_csv("../data/combined_data.csv")

states_map <- maps::map("state", region = ".",
                       plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE)|>  
  st_as_sf()

state_abre <- c( "alabama" = "AL", "arizona" = "AZ", "arkansas" = "AR",
  "california" = "CA", "colorado" = "CO", "connecticut" = "CT",
  "delaware" = "DE", "district of columbia" = "DC", "florida" = "FL",
  "georgia" = "GA", "idaho" = "ID", "illinois" = "IL", "indiana" = "IN",
  "iowa" = "IA", "kansas" = "KS", "kentucky" = "KY", "louisiana" = "LA",
  "maine" = "ME", "maryland" = "MD", "massachusetts" = "MA", "michigan" = "MI",
  "minnesota" = "MN", "mississippi" = "MS", "missouri" = "MO", "montana" = "MT",
  "nebraska" = "NE", "nevada" = "NV", "new hampshire" = "NH",
  "new jersey" = "NJ", "new mexico" = "NM", "new york" = "NY", 
  "north carolina" = "NC", "north dakota" = "ND", "ohio" = "OH",
  "oklahoma" = "OK", "oregon" = "OR", "pennsylvania" = "PA",
  "rhode island" = "RI", "south carolina" = "SC", "south dakota" = "SD",
  "tennessee" = "TN", "texas" = "TX", "utah" = "UT", "vermont" = "VT",
  "virginia" = "VA", "washington" = "WA", "west virginia" = "WV",
  "wisconsin" = "WI", "wyoming" = "WY")

states_map <- states_map |>
  mutate(State = recode(ID, !!!state_abre)) |> select(-ID)
#Inner join drop
full_data_with_state <- left_join(states_map, full_data , by = "State")

unique_months <- sort(unique(full_data_with_state$month))

month_variable = unique_months[2]

full_data_with_state_month <- full_data_with_state |> 
  filter(month == month_variable)


Gasplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_month, 
                  aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular)) +
  geom_sf() +
  scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Gas",
    subtitle = "Gas",
    fill = "Real Prices",
    caption = paste("Month:", as.character(month_variable)))


Gasplot

plotly::ggplotly(Gasplot)

```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#Idea:

# Read gas data
full_data <- read_csv("../data/combined_data.csv")

# Create sf object for US states
states_map <- maps::map(
  "state",
  region = ".",
  plot = FALSE,
  fill = TRUE
) |>
  st_as_sf()

# State abbreviations
state_abre <- c(
  "alabama" = "AL", "arizona" = "AZ", "arkansas" = "AR",
  "california" = "CA", "colorado" = "CO", "connecticut" = "CT",
  "delaware" = "DE", "district of columbia" = "DC", "florida" = "FL",
  "georgia" = "GA", "idaho" = "ID", "illinois" = "IL",
  "indiana" = "IN", "iowa" = "IA", "kansas" = "KS",
  "kentucky" = "KY", "louisiana" = "LA", "maine" = "ME",
  "maryland" = "MD", "massachusetts" = "MA", "michigan" = "MI",
  "minnesota" = "MN", "mississippi" = "MS", "missouri" = "MO",
  "montana" = "MT", "nebraska" = "NE", "nevada" = "NV",
  "new hampshire" = "NH", "new jersey" = "NJ", "new mexico" = "NM",
  "new york" = "NY", "north carolina" = "NC", "north dakota" = "ND",
  "ohio" = "OH", "oklahoma" = "OK", "oregon" = "OR",
  "pennsylvania" = "PA", "rhode island" = "RI",
  "south carolina" = "SC", "south dakota" = "SD",
  "tennessee" = "TN", "texas" = "TX", "utah" = "UT",
  "vermont" = "VT", "virginia" = "VA", "washington" = "WA",
  "west virginia" = "WV", "wisconsin" = "WI", "wyoming" = "WY"
)

# Rename state ID to abbreviation
states_map <- states_map |>
  mutate(State = recode(ID, !!!state_abre)) |>
  select(-ID)

# Join state map with gas data
full_data_with_state <- left_join(
  states_map,
  full_data,
  by = "State"
)

# Order months chronologically
unique_months <- sort(unique(full_data_with_state$month))

# Ensure months are ordered chronologically
full_data_with_state <- full_data_with_state |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = sort(unique(month))
    )
  )

# Consistent color scale
price_range <- range(
  full_data_with_state$MRA_Regular,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Interactive map with month slider
gas_plot2 <- plot_ly(
  data = full_data_with_state,
  type = "choropleth",
  locations = ~State,
  locationmode = "USA-states",
  z = ~MRA_Regular,
  frame = ~month,
  zmin = price_range[1],
  zmax = price_range[2],
  colorscale = "YlOrRd",
  colorbar = list(title = "Real Prices")
) |>
  layout(
    title = "Gas Prices by State",
    geo = list(scope = "usa")
  )

gas_plot2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
